```{r}
library(lme4)      # For mixed-effects models
library(lmerTest)  # For p-values with lmer()
library(tidyverse) # For data manipulation

```
# I must load my data first

```{r}
data <- read_delim("~/Documents/master_internship/outputs_final_data/final_df.csv", delim = ";")
data_session1 <- subset(data, session == "ses-mri01")
colnames(data)
head(data)
```
#I'm building up Congruency + RT here

```{r}
data$congruency_response <- factor(data$congruency_response)
data$volatility <- factor(data$volatility)
data$session <- factor(data$session)

```
#This is for all sessions
```{r}
model <- lmer(RT_s ~ congruency_response * time_since_switch * volatility * session + 
              (1 + congruency_response | subject), 
              data = data)

```
#But I am only interested in session 1 here 
```{r}
model_session1 <- lmer(RT_s ~ congruency_response * time_since_switch * volatility + 
                       (1 | subject), 
                       data = data_session1)

```

```{r}
summary(model_session1)
```
#Now let's see some plots

```{r}
ggplot(data_session1, aes(x = time_since_switch, y = RT_s, color = congruency_response)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  facet_wrap(~ volatility)


```
```{r}
ggplot(data_session1, aes(x = time_since_switch, y = RT_s, color = congruency_response)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  facet_wrap(~ volatility)

```
```{r}
ggplot(data_session1, aes(x = time_since_switch, y = RT_s, color = congruency_response)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ volatility) +
  theme_minimal()

```
#here following the SOP recommendations I want to find out whether my model is singular

```{r}
lme4::isSingular(model_session1, tol = 1e-4)

```
#Conservative estimation — just random intercepts to avoid overfitting, especially when you have singularity issues.

```{r}
model_summary <- lmer(
  RT_s ~ congruency_response * time_since_switch * volatility + 
         (1 | subject),
  data = data_session1
)

```


```{r}
summary(model_session1)$varcor

```
# This means that the average subject-level variation in baseline RT is about 0.105 seconds (since your DV is RT_s, i.e. in seconds). That’s substantial, meaning there is meaningful variation across subjects in their average RTs.
# Residual: This reflects the remaining within-subject variability, i.e. how much RT varies from trial to trial within subjects. It’s naturally larger, as trial-by-trial noise is usually high.


#I do this to try a more maximal model and then reduce 

```{r}
model_max <- lmer(RT_s ~ congruency_response * time_since_switch * volatility + 
                  (1 + congruency_response | subject), 
                  data = data_session1,
                  control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", calc.derivs = FALSE))

```

```{r}
rePCA(model_max)

```
```{r}
model_full <- lmer(RT_s ~ congruency_response * time_since_switch * volatility + 
                   (1 + congruency_response | subject), data = data_session1,
                   control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", calc.derivs = FALSE))


```

```{r}
model_simple <- lmer(RT_s ~ congruency_response * time_since_switch * volatility +
                     (1 | subject), data = data_session1)
```

#see which model is better
```{r}
anova(model_simple, model_full)
```
#fitted a linear mixed-effects model predicting response times (RT_s) from a fully crossed interaction between congruency_response, time_since_switch, and volatility, with a random intercept for subject (model_simple). 

#compared this to a model with both a random intercept and a random slope for congruency_response by subject (model_full), as recommended by Barr et al. (2013) to minimize inflated Type I error rates. 

#Although the full model yielded a singular fit warning (as confirmed by rePCA(), indicating a variance of zero for the slope term), a likelihood ratio test showed that it provided a significantly better fit to the data than the simpler model, χ²(2) = 17.67, p = .00015. Following best practices for prioritizing Type I error control, we retained the full model for interpretation while acknowledging the singularity and potential overparameterization. Both models are reported, and results are interpreted with caution.


#Now I move forward with Congruency & Objective performance 
```{r}
model_s1 <- glmer(accuracy  ~ congruency_response * time_since_switch +
                    (1 + congruency_response + time_since_switch | subject),
                  data = data_session1,
                  family = binomial)

```
```{r}
model_uncorrelated <- glmer(accuracy  ~ congruency_response * time_since_switch +
                              (1 + congruency_response + time_since_switch || subject),
                            data = data_session1,
                            family = binomial)

```
```{r}
rePCA(model_s1)

```
```{r}
model_conservative <- lmer(
  RT_s ~ congruency_response * time_since_switch * volatility + (1 | subject),
  data = data_session1
)

```

```{r}
summary(model_conservative)

```
#to check residuals: 
```{r}
plot(model_conservative)       # Residuals vs. fitted, scale-location, etc.
qqnorm(resid(model_conservative))
qqline(resid(model_conservative))

```
```{r}
plot(ggpredict(
  model_conservative, 
  terms = c("time_since_switch", "congruency_response", "volatility")
)) +
  ggtitle("Predicted RT by Time Since Switch, Congruency & Volatility") +
  theme_minimal()

```
# I want to plot the objectively correct response 
#For this apparently I need predictors for the predicted probability of a correct response (accuracy  = 1) as a function of time_since_switch, for each level of congruency_response.
```{r}
preds <- ggpredict(model_conservative, terms = c("time_since_switch", "congruency_response"))

```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

plot(preds) +
  labs(
    title = "Predicted Accuracy over Time Since Switch",
    x = "Time Since Switch",
    y = "Predicted Probability of Correct Response"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```
```{r}
library(dplyr)
data_session1 %>%
  group_by(congruency_response) %>%
  summarise(mean_accuracy = mean(accuracy , na.rm = TRUE))

```
```{r}
data_session1$congruency_response <- factor(data_session1$congruency_response, levels = c("congruent", "incongruent"))

```

```{r}
model_correct <- glmer(
  accuracy  ~ congruency_response * time_since_switch +
    (1 + time_since_switch | subject),
  data = data_session1,
  family = binomial
)

library(ggeffects)
plot(ggpredict(model_correct, terms = c("time_since_switch", "congruency_response"))) +
  labs(
    title = "Predicted Accuracy over Time Since Switch",
    x = "Time Since Switch",
    y = "Predicted Probability of Correct Response"
  )

```
